articles.title: Strange gamma-ray signal could unlock dark matter’s secrets
articles.summary: Researchers spotted an unusual gamma-ray signal in three galaxy clusters, which may be a telltale sign of dark matter – or some even more exotic phenomenon
articles.content:
Researchers spotted an unusual gamma-ray signal in three galaxy clusters, which may be a telltale sign of dark matter – or some even more exotic phenomenon

Could a strange burst of gamma rays be a sign of dark matter? National Science Foundation/LIGO/Sonoma State University/A. Simonnet

An unusual gamma-ray signal could be the most direct evidence of dark matter yet. However, the signal could also be the result of a telescope anomaly or produced by something even stranger than dark matter.

Dark matter forms the bones of much of our universe, driving how galaxies cluster, for example. It also far outweighs all the visible matter, yet for decades researchers have puzzled over what exactly it is.

Part of the problem is that they cannot currently observe dark matter directly. Instead, they can only register its effect on its surroundings. A more direct line of investigation would be to detect particles produced when dark matter collides and annihilates with itself, which some theories suggest ought to happen. Now, Yun-Feng Liang at Guangxi University in China and his colleagues identified a gamma-ray signal that may be the result of this process.

Advertisement

They found the signal after analysing 15.5 years of data from the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope (FGST), looking at the Virgo, Fornax, and Ophiuchus galaxy clusters specifically. The researchers chose these galaxy clusters because they are known to contain large halos of dark matter, says Liang. The gamma-ray signal the team found there was shaped like a spike or a line, analogous to a burst of light of only one colour, which some theories predict is the result of dark matter annihilating itself.

“Discovering a sharp gamma-ray line would be the ultimate ‘smoking gun’ evidence proving the existence of dark-matter particles and revealing their properties in particle physics,” says team member Yi-Zhong Fan at the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Based on their statistical analysis of the data, the researchers estimated that there is less than a 1-in-10,000 chance that this signal is random cosmic noise or a purely coincidental pattern.

Yet, several questions remain before the team can declare a definitive discovery. Detecting dark-matter signatures in gamma rays has historically been difficult because the signals tend to be weak and can be confused with telescope errors. One promising gamma-ray signal from 2012, for example, proved to be exactly that. Zhao-Qiang Shen, also at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, who worked on the new study, says the team members performed a large number of tests to confirm the veracity of their signal, but some possibility of instrument error remains.

Moreover, while the new signal is clear when looking at the three galaxy clusters, it seems to vanish closer to the centre of our galaxy, where dark matter is dense, so it should also be annihilating itself and creating gamma rays.

“The fact that the signal lights up in distant clusters but remains silent in our own cosmic backyard is deeply peculiar,” says Liang. “If this is truly from dark matter, it suggests the particles must interact in a much more sophisticated way than conventional theories predict.” Alternatively, the signal could be coming from some even more rare or novel phenomenon, such as ultra-fast particle winds from exotic magnetized neutron stars.

“I find the result intriguing, but I would be quite cautious about interpreting it as evidence for dark matter,” says Juri Smirnov at Liverpool University in the UK. He says that looking at only one galaxy cluster instead of all three together increases the chances that the signal is a product of noise or a random pattern. And he is also worried about how unconventional a dark-matter process would have to be to produce this gamma-ray spike far away from us but not close to the centre of our galaxy. “This puts the standard dark-matter interpretation under considerable tension,” he says.

The team hopes that future telescope missions will add clarity to the situation, for instance the Very Large Area Gamma-ray Space Telescope, which was proposed several years ago and could collect more gamma rays with better resolution. By 2040, FGST will also have doubled its data set, which could further elucidate the nature of the odd gamma-ray spike, says Fan.

“If future telescopes confirm that this signal is genuine, it would represent a historic breakthrough. It would immediately reveal the mass of the elusive dark-matter particle and give physicists a concrete target to build the next generation of fundamental particle theories,” says Shen. “At the same time, it would force us to thoroughly rewrite our standard textbook models of dark matter.”

articles.personality_title: Scientists detect unusual gamma-ray signal that may reveal dark matter
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Dark matter is an invisible substance that makes up most of the universe’s mass. Scientists cannot see it directly, but they know it affects how galaxies form and move. For many years, researchers have tried to find direct proof of what dark matter really is.

**What happened** – A team led by Yun-Feng Liang analyzed 15.5 years of data from the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope. They focused on three galaxy clusters called Virgo, Fornax, and Ophiuchus, which have large amounts of dark matter. The team found a sharp burst of gamma rays, a type of high-energy light, that appears as a narrow spike. This signal might come from dark matter particles colliding and destroying each other, which some theories predict.

**Impact** – This gamma-ray spike is special because it could be the clearest sign of dark matter particles so far. If confirmed, it would help scientists understand the properties of dark matter and improve particle physics. The chance that this signal is just random noise is very low, less than 1 in 10,000. However, the signal does not appear near the center of our own galaxy, which is unusual and raises questions about how dark matter behaves.

**What’s next step** – Researchers will continue to study this signal and check for possible errors. Upcoming telescopes, like the proposed Very Large Area Gamma-ray Space Telescope, and more data from the Fermi telescope by 2040, could provide clearer answers. Confirming this signal would be a major breakthrough and could change current ideas about dark matter.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Scientists have found a rare gamma-ray signal in distant galaxy clusters that might be the first direct evidence of dark matter particles.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des scientifiques détectent un signal gamma inhabituel qui pourrait révéler la matière noire
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – La matière noire est une substance invisible qui compose la majeure partie de la masse de l’univers. Les scientifiques ne peuvent pas la voir directement, mais savent qu’elle influence la formation et le mouvement des galaxies. Depuis longtemps, ils cherchent une preuve directe de ce qu’est vraiment la matière noire.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Une équipe dirigée par Yun-Feng Liang a analysé 15,5 ans de données du télescope spatial Fermi Gamma-ray. Ils se sont concentrés sur trois amas de galaxies appelés Virgo, Fornax et Ophiuchus, connus pour contenir beaucoup de matière noire. L’équipe a découvert une brusque émission de rayons gamma, un type de lumière très énergétique, qui apparaît sous forme d’un pic étroit. Ce signal pourrait venir de particules de matière noire qui s’entrechoquent et s’annihilent, comme le prédisent certaines théories.

**Impact** – Ce pic gamma est important car il pourrait être la preuve la plus claire jusqu’à présent de particules de matière noire. Si cela est confirmé, cela aiderait les scientifiques à comprendre les propriétés de la matière noire et à améliorer la physique des particules. La probabilité que ce signal soit un simple bruit aléatoire est très faible, moins d’une chance sur 10 000. Cependant, ce signal n’apparaît pas près du centre de notre galaxie, ce qui est étrange et soulève des questions sur le comportement de la matière noire.

**Prochaine étape** – Les chercheurs vont continuer à étudier ce signal et vérifier d’éventuelles erreurs. De futurs télescopes, comme le Very Large Area Gamma-ray Space Telescope proposé, ainsi que plus de données du télescope Fermi d’ici 2040, pourraient apporter des réponses plus claires. Confirmer ce signal serait une avancée majeure et pourrait changer les idées actuelles sur la matière noire.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Des scientifiques ont trouvé un signal gamma rare dans des amas de galaxies lointains qui pourrait être la première preuve directe des particules de matière noire.
articles.personality_title_es: Científicos detectan señal inusual de rayos gamma que podría revelar la materia oscura
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La materia oscura es una sustancia invisible que constituye la mayor parte de la masa del universo. Los científicos no pueden verla directamente, pero saben que influye en cómo se forman y mueven las galaxias. Durante años, han intentado encontrar una prueba directa de qué es realmente la materia oscura.

**Qué pasó** – Un equipo liderado por Yun-Feng Liang analizó 15,5 años de datos del Telescopio Espacial de Rayos Gamma Fermi. Se enfocaron en tres cúmulos de galaxias llamados Virgo, Fornax y Ophiuchus, que contienen grandes cantidades de materia oscura. El equipo encontró un pico estrecho de rayos gamma, un tipo de luz muy energética, que podría venir de partículas de materia oscura que se chocan y se aniquilan, como predicen algunas teorías.

**Impacto** – Este pico de rayos gamma es especial porque podría ser la señal más clara de partículas de materia oscura hasta ahora. Si se confirma, ayudaría a los científicos a entender mejor las propiedades de la materia oscura y avanzar en la física de partículas. La posibilidad de que esta señal sea solo ruido aleatorio es muy baja, menos de 1 en 10,000. Sin embargo, la señal no aparece cerca del centro de nuestra galaxia, lo que es extraño y plantea preguntas sobre cómo se comporta la materia oscura.

**Próximo paso** – Los investigadores continuarán estudiando esta señal y buscando posibles errores. Telescopios futuros, como el propuesto Telescopio Espacial de Rayos Gamma de Área Muy Grande, y más datos del telescopio Fermi para el 2040, podrían dar respuestas más claras. Confirmar esta señal sería un gran avance y podría cambiar las ideas actuales sobre la materia oscura.

**Resumen en una frase** – Científicos han encontrado una señal rara de rayos gamma en cúmulos de galaxias distantes que podría ser la primera evidencia directa de partículas de materia oscura.

articles.personality_title: New astronaut vest cuts radiation exposure by half during solar storms
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Space travelers face dangerous radiation from solar storms, which can harm their health and equipment during missions outside Earth's protective atmosphere.

**What happened** – NASA tested a special vest on an uncrewed space mission that reduced astronauts’ radiation exposure by 50%. This vest is designed to protect astronauts during strong solar storms by blocking harmful particles.

**Impact** – This vest is important because it lowers the risk of radiation sickness and long-term health problems for astronauts. It also helps keep space missions safer, especially as plans grow for longer trips to the Moon and Mars.

**What's next step** – NASA plans to improve the vest’s design and test it on crewed missions. This could lead to new safety gear for astronauts on future space journeys.

**One-sentence takeaway** – NASA’s new radiation-blocking vest cuts astronaut exposure in half, making space travel safer during solar storms.
articles.personality_title_fr: Un nouveau gilet réduit de moitié l'exposition aux radiations des astronautes pendant les tempêtes solaires
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les voyageurs spatiaux sont exposés à des radiations dangereuses lors des tempêtes solaires, qui peuvent nuire à leur santé et à leur matériel en dehors de l'atmosphère protectrice de la Terre.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – La NASA a testé un gilet spécial lors d'une mission spatiale sans équipage, qui a réduit de 50 % l'exposition des astronautes aux radiations. Ce gilet est conçu pour protéger les astronautes pendant les fortes tempêtes solaires en bloquant les particules nocives.

**Impact** – Ce gilet est important car il diminue les risques de maladie liée aux radiations et les problèmes de santé à long terme pour les astronautes. Il contribue aussi à rendre les missions spatiales plus sûres, surtout avec les projets de voyages plus longs vers la Lune et Mars.

**Prochaine étape** – La NASA prévoit d'améliorer le design du gilet et de le tester lors de missions avec équipage. Cela pourrait conduire à de nouveaux équipements de sécurité pour les astronautes lors des futurs voyages spatiaux.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le nouveau gilet anti-radiations de la NASA réduit de moitié l'exposition des astronautes, rendant les voyages spatiaux plus sûrs pendant les tempêtes solaires.
articles.personality_title_es: Nuevo chaleco astronauta reduce a la mitad la exposición a la radiación durante tormentas solares
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los viajeros espaciales enfrentan radiación peligrosa de las tormentas solares, que puede dañar su salud y equipo durante misiones fuera de la atmósfera protectora de la Tierra.

**Qué pasó** – La NASA probó un chaleco especial en una misión espacial sin tripulación que redujo la exposición a la radiación de los astronautas en un 50%. Este chaleco está diseñado para proteger a los astronautas durante tormentas solares fuertes bloqueando partículas dañinas.

**Impacto** – Este chaleco es importante porque reduce el riesgo de enfermedades por radiación y problemas de salud a largo plazo para los astronautas. También ayuda a que las misiones espaciales sean más seguras, especialmente con planes para viajes más largos a la Luna y Marte.

**Próximo paso** – La NASA planea mejorar el diseño del chaleco y probarlo en misiones con tripulación. Esto podría llevar a nuevos equipos de seguridad para astronautas en futuros viajes espaciales.

**Resumen en una frase** – El nuevo chaleco bloqueador de radiación de la NASA reduce a la mitad la exposición de los astronautas, haciendo más segura la exploración espacial durante tormentas solares.
